title: Finite principal-open cover carrying pseudo-coherent localized module models
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring and let $M^\bullet$ be a cochain complex of $A$-modules. Write $X=\operatorname{Spec}(A)$ [def-pc-scheme] and $E=\widetilde{M^\bullet}$ in its derived category [def-pc-derived-category]. If $E$ is pseudo-coherent [def-pur-pseudo-coherent-complex], there exist $r\geq0$ and $f:\{0,\ldots,r-1\}\to A$ with $(f_0,\ldots,f_{r-1})=A$ such that, for every $i$, the scalar-extended complex $A_{f_i}\otimes_A M^\bullet$ is pseudo-coherent in the module derived category [def-pc-ring-pseudo-coherent-complex], that is, it is isomorphic to a bounded-above complex of finite free $A_{f_i}$-modules. Derived categories may be chosen independently for $A$, for sheaves on $X$ and its opens, and for the localization rings.

source.place: Tag 08E7 (perfect-lemma-pseudo-coherent-affine), finite standard-open cover and identification of localized module models; local finite-free characterization in Tags 08CB and 08E5

proof.text: Let $A$ be as in the statement and $E=\widetilde{M^\bullet}$. By [def-pur-pseudo-coherent-complex], each point has an open neighbourhood $U$ on which $E$ has a bounded-above finite-free model. Refine these neighbourhoods by standard opens. Since $\operatorname{Spec}(A)$ is quasi-compact, extract a finite cover $D(f_1),\ldots,D(f_r)$. The covering condition implies that the $f_i$ generate the unit ideal. The restriction of a finite-free model to a smaller open preserves its upper bound and all its finite ranks.

For each $f_i$, identify $D(f_i)$ with $\operatorname{Spec}(A_{f_i})$. By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-module-tilde-sections], restriction of $\widetilde N$ is the associated sheaf of $A_{f_i}\otimes_A N$, since their sections and restriction maps agree on the standard-open basis. This is natural in $N$, and therefore identifies the termwise restricted input complex with the tilde of the scalar-extended complex.

Each term of the restricted model is a finite free structure-sheaf module. The fully faithful tilde functor and its finite-sum comparison [lem-weil-pbc-affine-tilde-gamma-adjunction] lift these terms and their differentials to finite free $A_{f_i}$-modules. Faithfulness gives the differential-square-zero identities. The complex has the same upper bound as the sheaf model.

Both sheaf complexes have quasi-coherent cohomology. The full inclusion of the quasi-coherent derived category lifts their derived isomorphism, and [lem-pc-affine-qcoh-derived-equivalence] over $A_{f_i}$ reflects it to the module derived category. Thus each localized complex has the finite-free representative required by [def-pc-ring-pseudo-coherent-complex]. No ring-level gluing is performed in this lemma. For the zero ring the empty family generates the unit ideal and the local condition is vacuous.
